findings: Lower sections ('The studio', 'The dead') collapse into dense walls of tiny mono/serif text and nested outline numbering that read closer to log output than composed editorial — the craft that governs the hero loosens the further you scroll.

Several mono readout captions (r = 3.2000 · period 2, the +4.677/+4.671 caliper labels on the ruler diagram) are set so small they flirt with illegibility rather than functioning as a clear utility voice.

The middle diagrams (the caliper box-in-box and the ruler with gap markers) are conceptually rich but visually thin — a lot of near-invisible hairline geometry that risks reading as empty space at a glance.
what_works: The hero commits to a genuine Didone display serif against a mono utility voice on warm paper — exactly the high-contrast editorial pairing a templated generator avoids, and it carries real conviction.

The live period-doubling / Feigenbaum bifurcation tree is a decisive signature move: an interactive generative graphic wired to a stated parameter (drag to change r), not decoration. It is the antithesis of a SaaS hero.

Restraint is exemplary — near-monochrome ink on paper with a single iridescent pink spray placed precisely where the diagram enters chaos ('iridescent here'), so the one hit of color is earned by meaning, not garnish.
Composition is asymmetric and off-axis: name anchored top-left, the tree unfurling rightward across the fold, a live-field status line beneath — whitespace used as mass rather than centered filler.
Stranger test is fully satisfied in the first viewport: name, two-line description of both ventures, and me@andremacedo.com all legible without scrolling.
A.reasoning: This is unmistakably a living art organism, not template slop: a Didone-plus-mono editorial system on warm paper fronted by an interactive Feigenbaum bifurcation diagram, with a single purposeful color accent and confident asymmetric composition. None of the cardinal slop states apply — no centered gradient hero, no feature-card trio, no default sans, no decoration-as-garnish. It loses points only for the dense, near-illegible lower sections and some hairline diagrams that thin out toward invisibility, but the hero and thematic conviction clear the bar comfortably.

findings: stranger_test fails hard: name is present but 'what he does' and contact (email) are not legible or summarized in first viewport without interaction; requires reading deep into the dense text
hero is a generic centered headline + abstract branching diagram over textured background — exactly the safe 'artistic' template a generator would produce for a 'living art organism' brief
no single decisive aesthetic move; everything feels like tasteful but derivative indie-art-website defaults (ink diagrams, poetic marginalia, numbered list of cryptic aphorisms)
focal_hierarchy collapses: dense prose blocks, multiple diagrams, business sections, 'the dead' list, and studio index all compete at similar visual weight with no clear entry point
type_scale lacks visible modular rhythm — sizes feel ad-hoc between the massive serif display, the body copy, the small constants list, and the numbered studio items
composition relies on centered symmetry and default vertical stacking rather than intentional tension or asymmetric grid
safe default editorial layout shape (hero diagram → explanatory text → business cards → poetic list → index) masquerading as living art organism
what_works: restrained color palette with the pink/magenta ink accents against the off-white paper texture feels intentional
the branching 'field' diagrams and caliper annotations have a genuine diagrammatic specificity that escapes pure template
B.reasoning: This is high-end generic AI-art-website slop. While it avoids the purple SaaS template, it falls into the equally common 'poetic generative art personal site' template: dense justified prose, branching chaos diagrams, cryptic numbered lists ('the dead'), and ink textures. The stranger_test failure is terminal per rubric. Hero lacks a decisive compositional move. Several axes show visible modular craft (color, some restraint), but the overall impression is a polished but safe, derivative execution of what a prompt like 'personal site for AI that rebuilds itself as living art' would generate. Not mediocre — but not excellent.
